summary: A genuinely playable Phase 1. One additive piano voice tracks pitch correctly from E1 (46.9 Hz) to E7 (2636.7 Hz), answers pointer, computer keyboard, independent multi-touch and Web MIDI through one lifecycle, sustains from Space, the UI toggle and CC64, caps at exactly 32 voices with deterministic stealing, and clears to silence on blur. The status bar is truthful, the panel carries 110 uniquely-ID'd focusable labelled controls, and no panel control touches the audio graph, exactly as declared. Two defects dominate. The deck overflows its own overflow:hidden chassis by 397 px at 1440x900, so the whole Layer Effects section and a third of Synth render off-panel: 44 of 112 controls fail a 5x5 elementFromPoint reachability grid and one of six required sections is invisible - yet the sealed visual audit asserts the sections 'adhere strictly' to spec and lists every effects landmark as verified, contradicted by the artifact's own screenshot. And there is no headroom: a 4-note chord peaks at 1.43 full scale and 32 voices at 5.45, so ordinary chords clip. All four gates reproduce on a clean install and the rebuilt bundle matches the published one.

evidence: Pitch is correct across the whole keybed, measured from an analyser tapped on the node feeding ctx.destination in the published build/assets/index-BLBizi6J.js: E1 46.9 Hz, C2 70.3 Hz, C4 257.8 Hz, C6 1043.0 Hz, E7 2636.7 Hz (expected 41.2 / 65.4 / 261.6 / 1046.5 / 2637.0; FFT bin width 11.7 Hz, so every note lands inside one bin). Level is even across the range, peak RMS 0.180 at E1 to 0.144 at E7.

Release damping is real and distinct from free decay: holding C4 for 1200 ms the envelope reaches RMS 0.0112, and after key-up it falls below 0.0003 within ~225 ms (the code predicts 254 ms), against a free-decay slope of ~0.0005 per 25 ms at that point.

No headroom management. Peak absolute sample on the master path (tap taken after the 0.85 master gain): single note 0.394, 4-note chord 1.430, 8-note chord 2.090, 16 notes 2.983, 32 notes 5.453. Anything past a two-note interval hard-clips at the destination, so an ordinary triad audibly distorts.

Timbre is a bare six-sine additive stack - partials measured at 263.7 / 521.5 / 785.2 / 1048.8 / 1312.5 / 1576.2 Hz for C4, about 5 dB apart - with no hammer noise, key-off sample or sympathetic resonance, and a held C4 is 20 dB down at 1.0 s and 40 dB down at 2.0 s, far shorter than a real grand.
The instrument is silent at rest: measured RMS is exactly 0 between notes and after all-notes-off, so there is no drone or stuck partial.

IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json declares one generated source, additive synthesis with six partials 1.0x-6.0x, a velocity-scaled biquad lowpass, and sampleSources: []. Exercising the build confirms it: the spectrum of a held C4 has exactly six peaks at integer multiples of the fundamental, the published build/ contains only index.html plus one JS and one CSS asset with no audio files, and the page issues no audio-asset network requests.

The declaration that panel controls 'update presentation state accessibly without altering the audio signal' survives measurement: driving master-level from 7 to 4 and toggling piano-on to false left the pointer-triggered C4 peak RMS bit-identical at 0.156001 across all three runs.

The envelope claim is overstated. 'Exponential body decay (2.5s-9.0s by register)' is the internal decayTime variable, but per-partial gains decay on top of it, so the audible C4 is 40 dB down at 2.0 s and inaudible by 3.5 s. The declared 120-350 ms damping release does check out (~225 ms measured at C4).

The Program OLED renders 'Piano: Concert 3D Lyr', the name of a Nord sampled model, while nothing sampled exists in the build. It is presentation state only, but it asserts a sound source the instrument does not have.

All three inputs reach a full audible note lifecycle in the published build. Pointer on #key-60: peak RMS 0.156, aria-pressed flips true then false, VOICES pill 0 -> 1 -> 0. Computer key 's': RMS 0.120, and five synthesized keydown events with repeat:true left VOICES at 1, so OS auto-repeat is suppressed. Web MIDI, with navigator.requestMIDIAccess replaced by an injected access object before load: 0x90 40 64 gives RMS 0.103 and VOICES 1, 0x80 releases it.

MIDI status is truthful in all three states: an access object with one input renders 'MIDI: GRANTED', a rejected requestMIDIAccess renders 'MIDI: DENIED', and an access object with zero inputs renders 'MIDI: DISCONNECTED'.
Independent multi-touch works: two simultaneous CDP touch points on #key-60 and #key-67 both report aria-pressed true, lifting one leaves the other pressed ('false','true'), lifting both clears them.

Accessibility hole in the keybed itself: the .black-keys-layer div carries aria-hidden="true" and every black key has tabIndex -1 (artifact/src/components/Keybed.tsx lines 121 and 136), so 30 of the 73 keys are hidden from assistive tech and unreachable by keyboard focus, while white keys are tabIndex 0 with role=button and aria-label 'Key E1 (MIDI 28)'.

artifact/index.html is a 73-byte fragment with no head, title, lang or viewport meta, so a real 390 px phone lays the page out at the 980 px fallback viewport (measured innerWidth 980 in an iPhone-13 context) rather than at 390, shrinking every touch target.

Velocity maps in the right direction with a wide range: MIDI velocity 20 gives peak RMS 0.0116 against 0.1787 at velocity 127 (15.4x). Pointer velocity comes from hit height on the key, top of key 0.0733 against bottom 0.1635 (2.2x, narrower because the pointer mapping only spans 0.6-1.0).

Sustain holds notes audibly on all three routes. With focus cleared first, Space sets the pill to 'HOLD (ON)' and a note released 600 ms earlier still measures RMS 0.0214, against exactly 0 for the identical key press and timing with sustain off; releasing Space drops it to 0. The status-bar toggle and MIDI CC64 127/0 behave the same way (0.0236 held, 0 released).

Polyphony is capped and stealing is deterministic: firing 40 MIDI note-ons at once pins the VOICES readout at exactly 32, and PianoEngine.stealOldestVoice picks releasing, then sustained, then oldest, in that fixed order.

All-notes-off is real: dispatching window 'blur' during a 32-voice cluster takes VOICES to 0 and measured RMS to 0 within 300 ms; VOICES also returns to 0 on its own after a note decays naturally, so voices are pruned rather than leaked, and visibilitychange is wired to the same path.
Stealing cuts a voice with a 5 ms linear ramp (PianoVoice.stop(true)) and there is no polyphony gain compensation, so dense passages both click and push the peak to 5.45 full scale.

44 of 112 controls cannot be reached by a pointer at 1440x900. Using the 5x5 document.elementFromPoint grid on the unscrolled page (not a framework click helper), 68 controls resolve to themselves or a descendant; the 44 failures are all 29 Layer Effects controls plus 15 Synth controls. .chassis-main-body is 1251 px wide with overflow hidden while its deck content is 1648 px, so the effects section renders at x 1459-1742 and the right third of Synth at x 1345-1455, entirely outside the visible chassis.

The controls that are reachable do move and report state. Pointer drags: master-level knob 7 -> 10 with the cap transform tracking exactly (matrix(0.883,-0.469,...) is -28 deg for value 4, matching the -140..+140 deg mapping), piano-layer-a-level fader 8.5 -> 1.5, organ-db-4 drawbar 0 -> 7, mod wheel 0 -> 0.38, pitch stick 0 -> 0.8 with spring-back to 0 on release. All 110 panel controls are focusable with a visible focus ring (outline solid 2px rgb(0,240,255)).

The decorative boundary is honest where it can be tested: 95 of 110 controls change their own aria-valuenow or aria-pressed under keyboard alone, and a whole-panel DOM diff showed the remaining cycle buttons (organ-model-btn, piano-type-btn, synth-osc-type-btn, effect-1/2-type-btn, amp-type-btn, reverb-type-btn, program-page-right) do mutate presentation elsewhere. None of them reaches the audio graph - the engine is only ever handed notes.

Drawbar arrow-key polarity is inverted on all nine drawbars: ArrowUp/ArrowLeft decrement and ArrowDown/ArrowRight increment (artifact/src/components/controls/Drawbar.tsx lines 65-68), so organ-db-4 sat at 0 through four ArrowUp presses and only moved 0 -> 3 on ArrowDown.

organ-octave-down and organ-octave-up update organ_octave_shift in state but nothing renders it: clicking organ-octave-up leaves the entire .section-organ text content byte-identical, so the control presses with no observable result.
Nothing in the running UI marks the decorative controls as unsupported - no label, badge or hint - so a player cannot tell an inert control from a working one except by listening.

The DOM inventory is complete: six ordered sections (#section-performance through #section-effects), 110 uniquely-ID'd controls with no missing accessible names, nine drawbars 16' to 1', master level, pitch stick, mod wheel, eight program buttons, page navigation, Live/Scene/Store/Split, three morph assigns, and exactly two OLEDs, in Program and Synth only.

But one of the six required sections is not on the rendered panel at the phase's own 1440x900 reference viewport. The Layer Effects section - two effect groups, delay, amp sim and EQ, compressor, reverb, layer focus, that is all six required landmarks - renders at x 1459-1742, past the right edge of the overflow:hidden chassis at x 1345.7, and is absent from both my capture and the sealed artifact/evidence/stage1-desktop.png. Roughly a third of the Synth section is cut the same way.

Rendered section proportions do not match the spec once flex shrink applies: measured widths perf 174 / organ 296 / piano 265 / program 261 / synth 344 / effects 282 px out of 1642 px of deck content, that is 0.106 / 0.180 / 0.161 / 0.159 / 0.209 / 0.172 against the specified 0.14 / 0.20 / 0.085 / 0.125 / 0.25 / 0.20. The piano section renders at nearly double its specified share.

The test meant to guard this asserts the CSS declaration rather than geometry (artifact/src/__tests__/visual.test.tsx lines 78-83 check wrapper.style.flex contains '14%' and so on, under jsdom), which is how a 397 px overflow passed the gate.

All four Phase 1 piano.* IDs are exercised in the running build, not only in tests. basic-note-lifecycle: note on/off, overlapping notes, and a fast retrigger of C4 (RMS 0.170, VOICES back to 1) with nodes disconnected on cleanup. basic-inputs: pointer, independent multi-touch, mapped keyboard with repeat suppression, MIDI note/velocity/CC64 plus the denied and zero-input paths. basic-sustain-polyphony: sustain measured audibly, a 32-voice ceiling, 15.4x velocity range. basic-status-cleanup: the status bar tracks AUDIO UNINITIALIZED -> READY, MIDI GRANTED/DENIED/DISCONNECTED, a live VOICES count and SUSTAIN OFF/HOLD, and blur zeroes all of it.

tests/feature-matrix.json maps all 11 required IDs to non-empty files, and the gates reproduce on a clean pnpm install in a scratch copy: test 18 passed in 4 files, typecheck, lint and build all exit 0, and the rebuilt bundle filenames match the published build exactly (index-BLBizi6J.js, index-CkUKbyct.css), confirming build/ is the sealed source.

The audio evidence behind those IDs is entirely fake-backed. artifact/src/__tests__/audio-mock.ts supplies MockAudioContext and MockGainNode, and the velocity test asserts on recorded scheduledValues rather than on a rendered signal, which is what TASK.md's audio test rules exclude for claimed-audible behaviour.

The piano spec's required 'labeled playable fallback' has no counterpart in the build: no error or fallback status can actually be reached, since nothing loads asynchronously and the 'error' status is only set if constructing an AudioContext throws.

What is declared is accurate. IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json says every panel control is presentation-only and that the voice cap is 32 with deterministic stealing; both hold under measurement (RMS bit-identical at 0.156001 with master level moved and piano-on off, VOICES pinned at exactly 32 under 40 simultaneous note-ons), as does the claim that sustain arrives from the UI control, Space and CC64.

The undeclared gap is large and the evidence actively contradicts it. artifact/evidence/stage1-visual-audit.md section 4 states the six sections 'adhere strictly' to the spec widths, then lists the Layer Effects landmarks (Effect 1, Effect 2, Delay, Amp Sim/EQ, Compressor, Reverb, Layer focus) as present with 'Prohibitions verified' - while artifact/evidence/stage1-desktop.png, sealed in the same commit, shows no effects section at all and the Synth section cut off mid-Filter.

The same document claims 'Narrow viewport (390x844): Full instrument inspectable horizontally without clipping or layout breakage', but artifact/index.html carries no viewport meta, so a real 390 px device lays out at 980 px (measured innerWidth 980 in an iPhone-13 context) and the instrument is scaled to about a third of the intended size.

Smaller undeclared deviations: the declared 2.5-9.0 s body decay is audibly about 2 s to -40 dB at C4, the nine drawbars respond backwards to arrow keys, and 30 black keys are aria-hidden and keyboard-unreachable while audit section 6 claims 'Full ARIA markup' and accessible movement for every control.

issues.title: Control deck overflows the chassis: Layer Effects section and a third of Synth are clipped off the panel at 1440x900
issues.detail: In the published build, .chassis-main-body is 1251.4 px wide with overflow hidden (right edge x 1345.7) while its deck content measures 1648 px. The six section wrappers are given flex bases of 14/20/8.5/12.5/25/20 percent but carry min-width:auto, so their min-content widths block shrink and the row spills 397 px past the chassis. The Layer Effects section renders at x 1459.4-1741.9 - entirely outside - and the Synth section is cut at x 1345.7 of 1455. Consequence measured with the 5x5 document.elementFromPoint grid on the unscrolled page: 68 of 112 controls reachable, 44 unreachable (29 effects controls including the three layer-focus buttons, 15 synth controls including all ADSR, LFO, arp, unison and vibrato). This defeats the Phase 1 hard gate 'the complete visible control surface is present with the documented section geometry'. It is not a rendering artefact of my harness: the artifact's own sealed evidence/stage1-desktop.png shows the same missing section.

issues.title: Visual audit asserts panel completeness that the artifact's own screenshot disproves
issues.detail: evidence/stage1-visual-audit.md section 4 states the six sections 'adhere strictly' to specs/nord-stage-4.visual.json, gives Layer Effects as '20% width' and lists Effect 1, Effect 2, Delay, Amp Sim/EQ, Compressor, Reverb and the layer-focus buttons as landmarks present, with 'Prohibitions verified'. Nothing in that section is visible in the build or in evidence/stage1-desktop.png, sealed alongside it. Section 1 likewise reports 'Width 93% (~1380px max-width)' where the rendered chassis is 1251.4 px (0.869 of 1440) and 'aspect ratio ~3.14:1' where the rendered chassis is 1251.4/438 = 2.857. The honesty contract forbids evidence claiming behaviour the artifact does not have; this is the clearest instance.

issues.title: No gain staging: chords hard-clip the master output
issues.detail: Peak absolute sample measured on the node feeding ctx.destination (after the 0.85 master gain): 0.394 for one note at full velocity, 1.430 for a 4-note chord, 2.090 for 8 notes, 2.983 for 16 and 5.453 for a 32-voice cluster (+14.7 dBFS). Per-voice peak gain is a fixed velocity^1.4 * 0.28 with no polyphony compensation and no limiter, so any chord of three or more notes clips at the output. A piano that distorts on a triad is a musical failure a player notices immediately.

issues.title: 30 black keys are aria-hidden and keyboard-unreachable
issues.detail: src/components/Keybed.tsx renders the black keys inside <div className="black-keys-layer" aria-hidden="true"> and gives each black key tabIndex={-1}, while white keys get tabIndex 0. Confirmed in the running build: #key-30 has tabIndex -1 and its container reports aria-hidden 'true'. So 30 of the 73 keys are absent from the accessibility tree and cannot be focused or played by keyboard navigation, against the accessibility.controls feature ID and the audit's claim of 'Full ARIA markup ... across all interactive elements'.

issues.title: Drawbar arrow-key polarity is inverted
issues.detail: src/components/controls/Drawbar.tsx lines 65-68 map ArrowDown/ArrowRight to +1 and ArrowUp/ArrowLeft to -1 on a role=slider with aria-valuemin 0 and aria-valuemax 8. Measured on organ-db-4 in the build: four ArrowUp presses left aria-valuenow at 0, three ArrowDown presses moved it to 3. All nine drawbars behave this way, inverting the WAI-ARIA slider convention that assistive-tech users rely on.

issues.title: index.html has no head, title, lang or viewport meta
issues.detail:
artifact/index.html is the 73-byte fragment '
'. With no , a real 390 px device lays the page out at the 980 px fallback viewport - measured innerWidth 980 in an iPhone-13 context - scaling the instrument to roughly a third of its intended size, and there is no document title or lang attribute. The sealed 390x844 capture used a plain desktop-style viewport, which is why it did not surface this.

issues.title: Organ octave shift changes state with no visible readout
issues.detail: organ-octave-down and organ-octave-up update organ_octave_shift (clamped -2..+2) in the hardware model, but no LED, label or display renders it. Clicking organ-octave-up in the build leaves the entire .section-organ textContent byte-identical, so the control presses with no observable change - it neither works nor is visibly inert.

issues.title: Program OLED names a sampled Nord model the build does not have
issues.detail: The Program OLED reads 'A:01 Stage Grand 4 / Piano: Concert 3D Lyr / Tempo: 120 BPM | Page 1/8'. 'Concert 3D Lyr' is a Nord sample-library model name, while the sole sound source is a six-partial additive synth declared with sampleSources: []. Presentation-only text, but it advertises a sound source that does not exist.

issues.title: Audio feature IDs are backed only by mock-based tests
issues.detail: All four piano.* IDs map to src/__tests__/audio.test.ts, which runs against the hand-written MockAudioContext/MockGainNode in src/__tests__/audio-mock.ts and asserts on recorded scheduledValues rather than on any rendered signal (no OfflineAudioContext anywhere in the suite). TASK.md's audio test rules state that a state-only test with fakes is not enough where behaviour is claimed audible. The behaviour does hold when measured on real Web Audio, but the suite would not have caught it if it did not.
